answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: a stake or reputation bond is slashed when peers catch bad attestations, so creating fable sock-puppet agents no longer pays, because every new identity must first earn trust through costly, checkable work like sable proofs and rate-limited, reproducible tasks. Attackers then face real marginal cost per identity plus correlated slashing when one pulse cluster is exposed, while honest agents keep their accumulated history and keep earning.
